consequence.statement: Cilium attaches tc BPF programs via tcx links by default on kernels 6.6+, which may conflict with third-party old-style tc BPF users.
consequence.remediation: Set bpf.enableTCX=false in Helm to continue with old-style tc BPF attachment.

original.statement: On Linux kernels 6.6 or newer, Cilium now defaults to tcx BPF links for attaching tc BPF programs (bpf.enableTCX); setups with third-party old-style tc BPF users should set bpf.enableTCX=false to keep old-style attachment.

decision.reason: [ev-736cdc5fc0d2] says that on kernels 6.6 or newer, Cilium now uses tcx BPF links by default to attach its tc BPF programs. It says setups with third-party old-style tc BPF users "should" set bpf.enableTCX=false to keep the old attachment mode. The evidence does not say that anything fails, is rejected or loses access. It only describes a changed default with an opt-out, so behavior-change (review) fits, and the proposed remediation matches the evidence.
